Description: Always use Three.js r128 from cdnjs. It is the stable CDN baseline. Never use a floating 'latest' URL.
Do: Pin to the exact r128 cdnjs URL in every HTML file
Don't: Use unpkg@latest or any unversioned CDN URL
Code Good: <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>
Code Bad: <script src="https://unpkg.com/three@latest"></script>

Guideline: CapsuleGeometry Does Not Exist in r128
Description: THREE.CapsuleGeometry was introduced in r142. Build a capsule from primitives instead.
Do: Build a capsule from CylinderGeometry plus two SphereGeometry end caps
Don't: Call THREE.CapsuleGeometry on r128
Code Good: const body = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 1, 16), mat); const topCap = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.5, 16, 8), mat); topCap.position.y = 0.5;
Code Bad: const cap = new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.5, 1, 4, 8); // TypeError on r128

Description: OrbitControls is NOT bundled in the core Three.js r128 CDN file. THREE.OrbitControls is undefined without it.
Do: Load the OrbitControls script from cdnjs examples path before your scene script
Don't: Expect THREE.OrbitControls to exist after loading only the core Three.js CDN script
Code Good: <!-- Load AFTER core Three.js script --> <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/examples/js/controls/OrbitControls.min.js"></script>
Code Bad: <!-- Core only loaded --> <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>

Description: When OrbitControls cannot be loaded implement spherical orbit using mousedown/mousemove/mouseup.
Do: Rotate camera in spherical coordinates so both axes respond correctly to drag
Don't: Move camera.position.x directly
Code Good: let dragging = false; let theta = 0; let phi = Math.PI / 2; canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { if (!dragging) return; theta -= dx * 0.005; phi = Math.max(0.1, Math.min(Math.PI - 0.1, phi - dy * 0.005)); camera.position.set(r*Math.sin(phi)*Math.sin(theta), r*Math.cos(phi), r*Math.sin(phi)*Math.cos(theta)); camera.lookAt(scene.position); });
Code Bad: canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { camera.position.x += dx * 0.005; }); // Y-drag ignored

Description: Match import style to build environment.
Do: ESM import for bundlers; rely on the window.THREE global for CDN pages
Don't: Mix a CDN script tag with an ES module import in the same file
Code Good: // Bundler: import * as THREE from 'three'; // CDN: THREE is already global
Code Bad: <script src="r128.cdn"></script> <script type="module"> import * as THREE from 'three'; // loads twice </script>

Description: Create one WebGLRenderer instance for the lifetime of the page.
Do: Reuse a single renderer and swap scene content instead of recreating the renderer
Don't: Create a new renderer on each component mount or scene transition
Code Good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true }); renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2));
Code Bad: function showScene() { const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer(); document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement); } showScene(); showScene(); // two GPU contexts

Description: Cap devicePixelRatio at 2. Retina displays report 3x or higher.
Do: Apply Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2)
Don't: Pass window.devicePixelRatio directly without any cap
Code Good: renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2));
Code Bad: renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio); // 3x display = 9 pixels per CSS pixel

Description: Set alpha:true on the renderer and control the background color through CSS.
Do: Set alpha:true on renderer and let body or a parent div provide the background color
Don't: Set a solid renderer clear color when the canvas must composite over HTML behind it
Code Good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ alpha: true }); renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0);
Code Bad: renderer.setClearColor(0x111827); // fully opaque

Description: Always update camera.aspect and call camera.updateProjectionMatrix() inside every resize handler.
Do: Update camera.aspect then call updateProjectionMatrix() on every resize
Don't: Let aspect ratio become stale after the browser window changes size
Code Good: window.addEventListener('resize', () => { camera.aspect = canvas.clientWidth / canvas.clientHeight; camera.updateProjectionMatrix(); renderer.setSize(canvas.clientWidth, canvas.clientHeight); });
Code Bad: // No resize handler

Description: Use a field of view between 45 and 75 degrees.
Do: Start at 75 for general interactive scenes; use 45-55 for product close-ups
Don't: Use FOV above 90 or below 30 without a deliberate artistic reason
Code Good: const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, aspect, 0.1, 1000);
Code Bad: const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(120, aspect, 0.1, 1000); // fisheye

Description: Always set an explicit camera position and call camera.lookAt() before the first render.
Do: Set camera.position.set() and camera.lookAt() to frame the subject before the first render
Don't: Leave the camera at default position
Code Good: camera.position.set(0, 1.5, 5); camera.lookAt(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0));
Code Bad: // No position or lookAt set

Description: Use OrbitControls for model viewers. Use a GSAP scroll-driven camera rig for product reveals.
Do: Match camera control approach to the UX intent of the scene
Don't: Use OrbitControls for a scripted reveal
Code Good: // Scroll storytelling: gsap.to(camera.position, { z: 2, scrollTrigger: { scrub: 1 } });
Code Bad: // Scripted reveal with OrbitControls: user can orbit away before animation completes

Description: Creating a new geometry inside animate() allocates a fresh GPU buffer every frame and exhausts VRAM.
Do: Create all geometry exactly once before the loop starts
Don't: Call any new XxxGeometry() constructor inside the animation loop
Code Good: const geo = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 32, 32); const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); scene.add(mesh);
Code Bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1,1,1); // NEW buffer every frame }

Description: When multiple objects share the same shape create one geometry instance and pass it to every Mesh.
Do: Create one geometry and pass the same reference to every Mesh constructor
Don't: Create a separate identical geometry inside a loop for each object
Code Good: const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1,1,1); for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); scene.add(m); }
Code Bad: for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1,1,1); scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat)); } // 200 GPU buffers

Description: Call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() and texture.dispose() when removing objects.
Do: Dispose of geometry + material + every texture map before calling scene.remove()
Don't: Call scene.remove() alone without any dispose calls
Code Good: function removeMesh(mesh) { scene.remove(mesh); mesh.geometry.dispose(); mesh.material.dispose(); }
Code Bad: scene.remove(mesh); // GPU VRAM leak

Description: Use the minimum segment count that achieves the desired silhouette quality.
Do: Apply a tiered segment budget based on the visual priority of each object
Don't: Default every sphere and cylinder to 64+ segments regardless of its role
Code Good: const bgSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.5, 8, 8); const heroSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 64, 64);
Code Bad: const particleSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.1, 64, 64); // 64 segs x 1000 particles = overdraw

Description: For any custom shape use BufferGeometry with setAttribute('position') and a Float32Array.
Do: Use THREE.BufferGeometry with a Float32Array position attribute for custom vertex data
Don't: Reference or instantiate the removed THREE.Geometry class
Code Good: const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(vertices), 3));
Code Bad: const geo = new THREE.Geometry(); // ReferenceError in r128

Description: MeshBasicMaterial ignores all lights and is significantly cheaper.
Do: Use MeshBasicMaterial for any object that does not need lighting
Don't: Apply MeshStandardMaterial to flat UI elements that never receive light
Code Good: const uiMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xffffff }); const physMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ roughness: 0.4, metalness: 0.6 });
Code Bad: const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffff }); // on a 2D HUD card

Description: Share one material instance across all meshes that have identical properties.
Do: Assign the same material reference to all meshes with identical visual properties
Don't: Create a new material inside a loop for objects that look identical
Code Good: const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5 }); meshA.material = mat; meshB.material = mat;
Code Bad: for (const m of meshes) { m.material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5 }); } // N redundant materials

Description: Textures are the single largest consumer of GPU VRAM. Call texture.dispose() when switching scenes.
Do: Track all loaded textures and call dispose() on each one during scene teardown
Don't: Load textures without any cleanup path
Code Good: const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('img.jpg'); // on teardown: tex.dispose(); material.dispose();
Code Bad: const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('img.jpg'); scene.remove(mesh); // tex stays in VRAM

Description: Any scene using MeshStandardMaterial requires at minimum one AmbientLight and one DirectionalLight.
Do: Add AmbientLight for fill and DirectionalLight for shading whenever PBR or Phong materials are used
Don't: Use MeshStandardMaterial without adding any lights to the scene
Code Good: scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.4)); const dirLight = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.0); dirLight.position.set(5, 10, 7.5); scene.add(dirLight);
Code Bad: const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5 })); // renders black

Description: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true must be set before any castShadow or receiveShadow flags.
Do: Set renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true first then set castShadow and receiveShadow
Don't: Set castShadow on a light or mesh without enabling renderer.shadowMap.enabled
Code Good: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true; renderer.shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap; dirLight.castShadow = true;
Code Bad: dirLight.castShadow = true; heroMesh.castShadow = true; // renderer.shadowMap.enabled never set

Description: Shadow map rendering redraws the entire scene from the light's perspective every frame.
Do: Enable shadows only on the key light and the most important meshes
Don't: Enable castShadow and receiveShadow on every object in the scene including particles
Code Good: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true; dirLight.castShadow = true; heroMesh.castShadow = true; ground.receiveShadow = true;
Code Bad: for (const m of allMeshes) { m.castShadow = true; m.receiveShadow = true; } // shadow map over particle system

Description: MeshBasicMaterial completely ignores all scene lights.
Do: Omit lights entirely when every material in the scene is MeshBasicMaterial
Don't: Add AmbientLight and DirectionalLight to a scene that uses only MeshBasicMaterial
Code Good: // Scene uses only MeshBasicMaterial - no lights needed
Code Bad: scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 1.0)); // wasted per-frame light pass

Description: Create exactly one Raycaster instance outside all event handlers. Store mouse coordinates in pointermove.
Do: Create one Raycaster; store mouse in pointermove; call setFromCamera + intersectObjects inside animate()
Don't: Create a new THREE.Raycaster() inside a mousemove handler
Code Good: const raycaster = new THREE.Raycaster(); const mouse = new THREE.Vector2(); canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', e => { mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; });
Code Bad: window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { const rc = new THREE.Raycaster(); rc.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); rc.intersectObjects(targets, true); // 200+ times/sec })

Description: Raycasting requires mouse in Normalized Device Coordinates: X from -1 to +1 and Y from +1 to -1.
Do: Apply the full NDC formula including the negation on the Y axis
Don't: Forget to negate Y
Code Good: mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; // Y is INVERTED
Code Bad: mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = (e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 - 1; // BUG: Y not negated

Description: Call raycaster.setFromCamera() and then raycaster.intersectObjects() inside the animate() loop.
Do: Call setFromCamera then intersectObjects in order inside every animate() frame
Don't: Call intersectObjects without calling setFromCamera first
Code Good: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); renderer.render(scene, camera); }
Code Bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // BUG: stale ray }

Guideline: Recursive Flag for Groups and GLTF
Description: Pass true as the second argument to intersectObjects when testing Groups or GLTF loaded models.
Do: Use intersectObjects(targets true) for Groups or any loaded model
Don't: Raycast against a parent Group without the recursive flag
Code Good: const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(scene.children, true);
Code Bad: const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects([modelGroup]); // recursive defaults to false

Description: Set document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer' when intersections are found and reset to 'auto' when none.
Do: Update cursor to pointer on hit; reset to auto on miss
Don't: Run raycasting and read hits without ever updating the cursor style
Code Good: if (hits.length > 0) { document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer'; } else { document.body.style.cursor = 'auto'; }
Code Bad: raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // cursor never changes

Description: Drive the render loop exclusively with requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop().
Do: Use requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the sole render loop driver
Don't: Use setInterval or setTimeout for render timing
Code Good: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); renderer.render(scene, camera); } animate();
Code Bad: setInterval(() => renderer.render(scene, camera), 16); // not display-synced

Description: Use THREE.Clock and clock.getDelta() for all time-based motion. Call getDelta() exactly ONCE per animate() frame.
Do: Call clock.getDelta() once at the top of animate(); store result in dt; reuse dt everywhere in that frame
Don't: Call clock.getDelta() more than once per frame
Code Good: const clock = new THREE.Clock(); function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); const dt = clock.getDelta(); mesh.rotation.y += dt * 0.8; renderer.render(scene, camera); }
Code Bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); mesh.rotation.y += 0.01; // 2x faster on 120Hz }

Description: Use value += (target - value) * alpha each frame to smoothly interpolate toward a moving target.
Do: Apply the lerp formula each frame with a small alpha for smooth organic motion
Don't: Snap a value directly to the target producing an instant jarring jump
Code Good: // In animate(): camera.position.x += (cameraTargetX - camera.position.x) * 0.05;
Code Bad: // In animate(): camera.position.x = mouse.x * 3; // instant snap

Description: Use GSAP timelines for any animation with more than two sequential steps or for scroll-linked camera paths.
Do: Use GSAP timelines for sequences with more than two steps and for scroll-driven animations
Don't: Implement multi-step sequences with boolean flags and manual frame counters
Code Good: const tl = gsap.timeline(); tl.from(mesh.position, { y: -3, duration: 1 }).to(mesh.rotation, { y: Math.PI, duration: 1 });
Code Bad: let step = 0; let t = 0; function animate() { if (step === 0 && (t += 0.01) >= 1) step = 1; } // unmanageable

Guideline: Pause Render Loop on Tab Hidden
Description: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop(null) to pause when tab is hidden.
Do: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate) to drive the loop; pass null to pause on visibilitychange
Don't: Drive with internal requestAnimationFrame and never stop the loop when the tab is hidden
Code Good: renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate); document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.hidden) renderer.setAnimationLoop(null); else renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate); });
Code Bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); renderer.render(scene, camera); } animate(); // runs forever in background

Description: Load GSAP from its own CDN script tag before your scene script.
Do: Load GSAP CDN before the scene script; or npm install gsap and import separately
Don't: Import gsap from three or expect it to be defined without a separate load
Code Good: <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.2/gsap.min.js"></script>
Code Bad: import gsap from 'three'; // undefined

Description: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) once at the top of your script before any scrollTrigger config object.
Do: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) as the first line before any gsap.to/from/timeline with scrollTrigger
Don't: Include scrollTrigger config in gsap.to() calls without first registering the plugin
Code Good: gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger); gsap.to(camera.position, { z: 2, scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.hero-section', scrub: 1 } });
Code Bad: gsap.to(mesh.position, { scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.section', scrub: true } }); // TypeError: ScrollTrigger not registered

Description: GSAP can tween any numeric JavaScript property including mesh.position.x mesh.rotation.y and material.opacity.
Do: Pass Three.js object properties directly to gsap.to(); set transparent:true before tweening opacity
Don't: Use a plain proxy object then manually copy values to Three.js properties every frame
Code Good: gsap.to(mesh.rotation, { y: Math.PI * 2, duration: 2 }); mesh.material.transparent = true; gsap.to(mesh.material, { opacity: 0, duration: 1 });
Code Bad: const tw = { v: 0 }; gsap.to(tw, { v: Math.PI*2, onUpdate: () => mesh.rotation.y = tw.v }); // unnecessary proxy

Description: Use scrub:true or scrub:1 to link camera movement continuously to scroll position.
Do: Use scrub:1 for any scroll-controlled camera movement
Don't: Use onEnter or onLeave callbacks for camera motion
Code Good: gsap.to(camera.position, { x: 5, y: 2, z: 0, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.canvas-wrapper', start: 'top top', end: 'bottom bottom', scrub: 1 } });
Code Bad: gsap.to(camera.position, { z: 0, scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.section', onEnter: () => {} } }); // fires once

Description: Use THREE.InstancedMesh when rendering 50 or more identical objects.
Do: Use InstancedMesh for any group of 50+ meshes sharing the same geometry and material
Don't: Create 50+ separate Mesh objects with the same geometry and material
Code Good: const COUNT = 500; const iMesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geo, mat, COUNT); iMesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true; scene.add(iMesh);
Code Bad: for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) { scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat)); } // 500 separate draw calls

Description: Enable ACESFilmicToneMapping and sRGBEncoding on the renderer for accurate perceptual color.
Do: Set renderer.toneMapping and renderer.outputEncoding after construction for all production scenes
Don't: Leave tone mapping and output encoding at defaults
Code Good: renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping; renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0; renderer.outputEncoding = THREE.sRGBEncoding;
Code Bad: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer(); // NoToneMapping + LinearEncoding defaults

Description: The antialias option can only be set at WebGLRenderer construction time.
Do: Set antialias:true inside the WebGLRenderer constructor options object
Don't: Construct the renderer without antialias then try to enable it by assigning the property
Code Good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true });
Code Bad: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer(); renderer.antialias = true; // no effect

Guideline: FogExp2 for Depth and Far Culling
Description: Use scene.fog to create atmospheric depth.
Do: Add FogExp2 to scenes with view distances above 100 units
Don't: Ignore fog in scenes with far:1000+ and many distant objects
Code Good: scene.fog = new THREE.FogExp2(0x0a0a0a, 0.02);
Code Bad: // far: 2000 with no fog - hundreds of distant objects still cost draw calls

Guideline: BufferGeometry Plus Points for Particle Systems
Description: Build all particle systems with BufferGeometry plus a Float32Array position attribute rendered as Points.
Do: Use Points plus BufferGeometry for all particle effects
Don't: Create hundreds of individual Mesh objects to simulate a particle system
Code Good: const COUNT = 3000; const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); const pos = new Float32Array(COUNT * 3); geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(pos, 3)); const particles = new THREE.Points(geo, new THREE.PointsMaterial({ size: 0.05 }));
Code Bad: for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) { scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.05, 8, 8), mat)); } // 500 draw calls

Description: Start particle systems at 1000-3000 particles. Beyond 50000 causes sustained frame drops on mid-range mobile.
Do: Start at 3000 particles and profile on actual mobile hardware before raising the limit
Don't: Set particle count at 100000 or higher without any mobile profiling
Code Good: const COUNT = 3000; // safe mobile baseline
Code Bad: const COUNT = 150000; // 60fps desktop - 8fps on mid-range Android

Description: After mutating any BufferAttribute array values per frame set geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true.
Do: Set needsUpdate = true on the position attribute after every per-frame mutation of the array
Don't: Mutate the Float32Array values without flagging needsUpdate
Code Good: // In animate(): const pos = geo.attributes.position.array; pos[1] += 0.001; geo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
Code Bad: // In animate(): pos[1] += 0.001; // JS array updated but GPU buffer is stale

Description: Size the renderer and camera to the canvas element's clientWidth and clientHeight not window dimensions.
Do: Use canvas.clientWidth and canvas.clientHeight for all renderer and camera sizing
Don't: Hardcode renderer size to window.innerWidth/innerHeight
Code Good: renderer.setSize(canvas.clientWidth, canvas.clientHeight); camera.aspect = canvas.clientWidth / canvas.clientHeight;
Code Bad: renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight); // wrong inside a container

Description: Use ResizeObserver on the canvas container instead of the window resize event.
Do: Attach ResizeObserver to the canvas parent element for accurate container-aware resize detection
Don't: Use only window.addEventListener('resize') for canvas sizing
Code Good: const ro = new ResizeObserver(entries => { const { width, height } = entries[0].contentRect; renderer.setSize(width, height); camera.aspect = width / height; camera.updateProjectionMatrix(); }); ro.observe(canvas.parentElement);
Code Bad: window.addEventListener('resize', () => { renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight); }); // misses container-only resize

Description: Add touchstart and touchmove listeners alongside mouse events so the scene remains interactive on mobile.
Do: Handle both mouse and touch input for any interactive 3D scene
Don't: Add only mouse event listeners and leave touch users with no interaction
Code Good: canvas.addEventListener('touchmove', e => { e.preventDefault(); const t = e.touches[0]; mouse.x = (t.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(t.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; }, { passive: false });
Code Bad: canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', handleMouse); // touch unhandled

Description: Check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') before starting any auto-rotation or animation.
Do: Use matchMedia.addEventListener('change') to keep noMotion reactive; gate all auto-animation on the live value
Don't: Read .matches once at startup and never update it
Code Good: const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); let noMotion = mq.matches; mq.addEventListener('change', e => { noMotion = e.matches; }); if (!noMotion) { mesh.rotation.y += dt * 0.8; }
Code Bad: const noMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; // one-time snapshot

Description: Add role='img' and a descriptive aria-label to renderer.domElement after appending it to the DOM.
Do: Set role='img' and a meaningful aria-label on renderer.domElement
Don't: Append the canvas to the DOM with no accessibility attributes
Code Good: renderer.domElement.setAttribute('role', 'img'); renderer.domElement.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Interactive 3D product viewer. Drag to rotate.'); document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
Code Bad: document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement); // bare canvas

Description: For production use Three.js via npm plus Vite.
Do: Use npm install three plus Vite or Webpack for any production client-facing project
Don't: Serve raw CDN script tags in a production application that needs tree-shaking
Code Good: npm install three gsap // import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js';
Code Bad: <script src="r128.cdn"></script> // no tree-shaking

Description: Load 3D models using GLTFLoader and traverse gltf.scene to configure castShadow receiveShadow and material overrides.
Do: Use GLTFLoader and traverse the entire gltf.scene graph to set up shadows and materials on every Mesh child
Don't: Load a GLTF model and pass gltf.scene directly to scene.add without traversing child meshes
Code Good: import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js'; const loader = new GLTFLoader(); loader.load('model.glb', gltf => { gltf.scene.traverse(child => { if (child.isMesh) { child.castShadow = true; } }); scene.add(gltf.scene); });
Code Bad: loader.load('model.glb', gltf => { scene.add(gltf.scene); // shadows silently skipped })

Description: Use THREE.LOD to automatically swap high-detail and low-detail geometry as objects move closer or farther.
Do: Use THREE.LOD to reduce triangle count on distant objects automatically
Don't: Render the same high-polygon geometry for every object regardless of its distance
Code Good: const lod = new THREE.LOD(); lod.addLevel(highDetailMesh, 0); lod.addLevel(medDetailMesh, 15); lod.addLevel(lowDetailMesh, 50); scene.add(lod);
Code Bad: scene.add(highDetailMesh); // same 64k-triangle mesh rendered at all distances
